solutions.check: 30 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 28 answers the paper printed; printed-crossing fills: 1-down

clue.text: A Tory grant to join the party

parts.note: C stands for Conservative, the party of the Tories
to cede is to grant or yield something to another

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician agrees to sign up with the party faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede to a treaty or agreement is formally to become a party to it, so the verb is joining.

clue.text: Monkey about — put in place — that's to the purpose

indicators.note: the monkey wraps around the 'put in place' word

parts.note: an ape is a monkey in the loose crossword sense
to posit is literally to place or set something in position

explanation.surface: A monkey messing about and being repositioned, apparently with good reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite means relevant and apt, exactly fitting the matter in hand.

clue.text: Nice car, new model — dangerously alluring

indicators.note: a new model of the letters means they are rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: An attractive car in a fresh version tempts the buyer into peril.
explanation.definitionFit: Circe the enchantress lured men and turned them into swine, so something Circean is perilously seductive.

clue.text: Hauled up unruly youth to be taken away

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' tells you the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: carted means hauled or carried
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a rebellious youth in 1950s Britain

explanation.surface: A rowdy teenager is dragged off and removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CARTED into DETRAC. A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress, a byword for trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Detracted, in its older sense, means withdrawn or removed, so it is a synonym of subtracted.

clue.text: Official information about posh dwelling house

indicators.note: the message wraps around the letter for posh, so 'about' signals one piece going round another

parts.note: a message is an official communication passing on information
U means upper-class, the classic label for posh usage

explanation.surface: A government bulletin concerning some grand residence.
explanation.walkthrough: U for 'posh' comes from the 1950s split of English usage into U (upper-class) and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal language a messuage is a house together with its outbuildings and land, a residence.

clue.text: Town strange Asiatic left for the church

parts.note: Eccles is a town in Greater Manchester, famous for its currant cakes

indicators.note: something strange is out of its normal state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd Asian visitor abandoned a northern town to join the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges ASIATIC into IASTICA. Eccles is a town near Manchester in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesiastical describes whatever relates to or belongs to the Christian clergy and its institutions.

clue.text: Hard to set in like this

indicators.note: the word 'to' is set inside the Latin for 'thus'

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mean 'written like this'

explanation.surface: A stubborn thing to get embedded in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic person is hardy and unflinching, enduring pain without complaint.

clue.text: Protein drink — there's none in the container

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer

indicators.note: the zero is placed inside the vessel

parts.note: an urn is a container, for tea or ashes
O, the figure zero, means none

explanation.surface: A protein shake with nothing left in the jug.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleurone is a protein found as granules in the outer layer of cereal seeds.

clue.text: Rank is all one has

definitions.meaning: a class or order in society
the whole property a person owns, especially at death

explanation.surface: A man's standing is all he owns.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a social class or order, and also a person's whole property and possessions.

clue.text: Stories well expressed, with changing characters

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or table talk about a person
grammatical means correctly expressed in good language

explanation.surface: Tales told elegantly, with a shifting cast of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' are letters, not people in the stories; ANA is a collection of anecdotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done by transposing letters to form new words involves letters swapping places, the clue's changing characters.

clue.text: Carthaginian holds a girl to be strait-laced

indicators.note: the Carthaginian word keeps the girl's name gripped inside it, so 'holds' is the container signal

parts.note: Punic is the adjective for ancient Carthage and its people
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man from ancient Carthage keeps a young woman under strict moral control.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone puritanical is rigidly strict in morals, which is what strait-laced describes.

clue.text: Public love things with green leaves

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, shown as the round letter O
vert is an old forest-law word for green vegetation growing in a woodland

explanation.surface: Romance among the leafy plants of the garden, all out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overt is done openly, in public view, not concealed.

clue.text: Woman, a hit in an affair

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
a bang is a blow or hit

explanation.surface: A woman gets struck during a romantic entanglement.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from 'the whole shebang', meaning the whole business or affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebang is an informal word for a matter, business or thing, so an affair in that general sense.

clue.text: Cutting, but about right

indicators.note: the word for 'but' goes around the letter for right, so 'about' marks the wrapping

parts.note: except means but, as in 'all but him' and 'all except him'

explanation.surface: A remark that is wounding, yet near enough correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like an adjective for a sharp remark; here it is a noun, a press cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting from a newspaper is an extract or passage taken out of a longer text.

clue.text: Point in wine doctrine

indicators.note: the compass point is placed inside the name of the wine

parts.note: tent is a dark red Spanish wine once used for communion
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A basic belief set out within the wine trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true, the core of a doctrine.

clue.text: The local birds take an old way round the rural diety

indicators.note: the old road goes round the rural god, so 'round' signals one piece enclosing another

parts.note: a via is a Roman road, so 'an old way' is A plus VIA
a faun is a Roman god of the countryside, half man and half goat; 'diety' is a printed misspelling of deity

explanation.surface: Local wildlife follows an ancient track around a country diet.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'diety', the setter's misspelling of 'deity'; read it as deity and the rural god is the FAUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Avifauna is the collective term for the bird life of a particular region.

clue.text: A concrete factor in assemblage

definitions.meaning: the crushed stone or gravel that is mixed into concrete
a collection or mass of things gathered together

explanation.surface: A component in a construction gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggregate is the sand and gravel mixed into concrete, and also a total gathered from many parts.

clue.text: Due, after upset, to be given special prominence

indicators.note: upsetting the letters scatters them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Something owed, once overturned, is put in the spotlight.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma tempts you to read 'after upset' as a time; 'upset' is the anagram signal working on the two words beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A news item that is featured is highlighted or made a main attraction.

clue.text: Lady in trouble with ladies generally

indicators.note: the titled woman is placed inside the word for trouble

parts.note: to be in a mess is to be in trouble
a dame is a titled lady

explanation.surface: A noblewoman gets into difficulties alongside her female companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesdames, the French plural of madame, is a polite form of address to women as a group.

clue.text: Nobody with number up can show high spirits

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' means the whole string is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: no one, written NO plus I, the Roman numeral for one
a tale is an old word for a count or number, as in a tally

explanation.surface: No one with a rising headcount can feel cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NO I TALE to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great joy and exhilaration, so a state of high spirits.

clue.text: Girl -in favour?

definitions.meaning: kindness or goodwill shown to someone

explanation.surface: A young woman asks whether she is in favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace is a girl's name, and grace also means goodwill or favour, as in 'by the grace of'.

clue.text: Girl page boy suited

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl, a page-boy and a lad are all well dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Adapted means made suitable or fitted for a purpose.

clue.text: Odds on strike, or prominent display

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds when a race begins
to lash is to strike with a whip

explanation.surface: A bet is placed on a workers' walkout or a big public show.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is the British bookmakers' term for the final odds on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a splash is to attract attention with a showy display, as in a front-page splash.

clue.text: Double back in match to get acclaim

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the word for match

parts.note: to pit one against another is to match them in a contest

indicators.note: the word for double is read backwards, 'back' turning it round

parts.note: dual means double, two-fold

explanation.surface: A doubles player returns during a game and wins applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaudits are expressions of praise or applause, so the word is a synonym for acclaim.

clue.text: The people in the side, mostly

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: Most of the population is on the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Demos is the Greek word for the common people, used for the populace as a political body.

clue.text: Batting out of turn — that's not quite correct

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
ex means out of or from, as in ex-directory
an act is a turn, a short performance on stage

explanation.surface: A cricketer going in to bat out of order is slightly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of turn' looks like one phrase meaning in the wrong order, but it splits into two separate pieces; 'turn' is a stage act.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexact is imprecise, falling short of being accurate.

clue.text: Verity has no need of proof

definitions.text: Verity has no need of proof

parts.words: Verity has no need of proof
parts.note: describes a self-evident truth accepted without demonstration, read straight as a definition; 'Verity' also looks like a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman named Verity doesn't need to show her evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement accepted as true without demonstration, a basic self-evident principle.

clue.text: Privilege, embracing current letter

indicators.note: the privilege word hugs the electrical abbreviation inside itself

parts.note: a charter is a granted privilege or right
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A special right that takes in the present letter of correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is a written symbol, such as a letter of an alphabet.

clue.text: Straight home in divine surroundings

indicators.note: the home word sits in the middle of the divine word, the clue's 'surroundings'

parts.note: holy means divine or sacred
a nest is a home, especially a cosy one

explanation.surface: Going directly home amid heavenly surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straight' looks like 'directly'; here it is an answer to a question, as in 'honestly?' 'straight up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking straight means speaking truthfully, without deceit, which is what the adverb conveys.

clue.text: We would accept old age, having stuck together

indicators.note: the contraction takes in the word for old age, so 'accept' signals containment

parts.note: we'd is the contraction of we would
eld is an archaic word for old age

explanation.surface: A couple willing to accept growing old after sticking it out together.
explanation.definitionFit: Welded metal parts are joined by fusion, so they are fixed or bonded together.
